rows.source: curated:the cell says identifier, the element that holds the DOI; DataCite 4.7 added SWHID as a relatedIdentifierType, so a SWHID is a related identifier
rows.comment: Only schema 4.7 and later have this type, and the schema does not say which relationType goes with it, so read the first related identifier of that type whatever its relationType. Older records have none.

rows.source: curated:no cell; DataCite has no repository property. Zenodo records the repository as a related identifier with relationType IsSupplementTo; bolognese's CodeMeta writer uses url, which holds the repository for DOIs registered from codemeta.json
rows.comment: IsSupplementTo is Zenodo's convention: keep the one whose relatedIdentifierType is URL on a forge host (often a tag URL, …/tree/v1.0). url is the DOI's landing page: on Zenodo and most repositories it is the record page, not the code, so use it only when it is on a forge host.

rows.source: curated:the cell says description, the XML element; in the REST JSON descriptions is a list, and the summary is the one with descriptionType Abstract. bolognese's CodeMeta writer takes the first description, which is the Abstract in most records
rows.comment: Other descriptionType values (Methods, TechnicalInfo, Other and so on) are not the description.

rows.source: curated:the cell says subject, the XML element; in the REST JSON subjects is a list of objects with a subject key
rows.comment: A subject may carry a subjectScheme (a controlled vocabulary such as FAST or MeSH); those are not free keywords.

rows.source: curated:the cell says publicationYear, a bare year; bolognese's writers give datePublished as the Issued date and use publicationYear only when there is none
rows.comment: publicationYear is a number (2023), dates[].date can be a full date or a range.

curated:the cell says dcterms:title; the path uses its bare local name because the grammar has no ':'
curated:the cell says dcat:version, which DCAT 3 added for the version name or identifier of a resource; the path is its local name, with owl:versionInfo after it, which Zenodo's DCAT export writes
curated:the cell says dcterms:creator; a dataset can have several creators, so the path is a list of its local name creator
rows.comment: The spec recommends a foaf:Agent as the value, so an element is an object or an IRI. A creator with only an IRI has no name sub-fields.

rows.source: curated:no cell; the spec types a creator as foaf:Agent, whose person form carries foaf:givenName
rows.comment: An agent that has only foaf:name has no given or family name here; the consumer then splits creator[].name.

rows.source: curated:no cell; the spec types a creator as foaf:Agent, whose person form carries foaf:familyName
rows.comment: An agent that has only foaf:name has no given or family name here; the consumer then splits creator[].name.

rows.source: curated:the cell says dcterms:identifier, which names the identifier of a resource and not of an agent; an ORCID is the agent's own IRI, so the @id of the creator node
rows.comment: The spec also allows adms:identifier on the agent for an ORCID given as a string; a consumer may read that when @id is absent.

rows.source: curated:the cell says dcterms:contributor; a list of its local name, as for creator
rows.comment: DCAT lists dcterms:contributor, dcterms:creator and dcterms:publisher as the standard properties for basic agent associations (section 13.1); prov:qualifiedAttribution with dcat:hadRole is for other roles, which a path cannot express.

rows.source: curated:same reasoning as author.givenName, under contributor
curated:same reasoning as author.familyName, under contributor
curated:same reasoning as author.@id, under contributor
curated:the cell says dcterms:license, which DCAT allows on the dataset and on each distribution; the path reads the dataset's, else a distribution's
rows.comment: The value is a dcterms:LicenseDocument, usually an IRI; the consumer converts between IRI and SPDX id. Zenodo's software records give the licence only on the distribution, as dct:rights with an SPDX adms:identifier, which this path does not read.

rows.source: curated:the cell says dcterms:identifier; the path is its local name. The software DOI is one of its values
rows.comment: dcterms:identifier is repeatable and untyped; a DOI is told from a SWHID by its spelling.

rows.source: curated:the cell says dcterms:identifier, which holds the DOI; DCAT has no property of its own for a SWHID
rows.comment: A record may still carry a SWHID as a second dcterms:identifier or as an adms:identifier; the consumer finds it by its swh:1: spelling.

rows.source: curated:the cell says dcat:accessURL, a property of dcat:Distribution that usually points at a landing page or a download, not a repository
curated:the cell says dcterms:description; the path is its local name
curated:the cell says dcat:keyword; the path is its local name
rows.comment: Repeatable: a single keyword may be a string rather than an array.

rows.source: curated:the cell says dcterms:issued, the date of formal issuance; the path is its local name
rows.comment: A date typed xsd:gYear, xsd:gYearMonth, xsd:date or xsd:dateTime; a record may give several (Zenodo gives a year and a date), so take the most precise. A typed literal may arrive as {"@value", "@type"}.

curated:the cell says revision, which belongs to doap:Version, not to the project; a project reaches a Version through doap:release, so the path is release[].revision
rows.comment: A project lists many releases; the consumer picks the newest, by doap:created or by revision order.

rows.source: curated:the cell says developer, but most DOAP files (Apache's, GNOME's) list only maintainer, so the path falls back to it
curated:no cell; DOAP people are foaf:Person nodes and the name most DOAP files give is foaf:name, one string
rows.comment: The consumer splits the name into given and family name; a node that has foaf:givenName and foaf:familyName can be read directly.

rows.source: curated:no cell; DOAP people are foaf:Person nodes and the name most DOAP files give is foaf:name, one string

rows.source: curated:no cell; DOAP has no ORCID property, but a foaf:Person node can be named by its ORCID IRI, which JSON-LD keeps as @id
rows.comment: Most DOAP files name people with a blank node, so this is often absent.

rows.source: curated:the cell says developer, which is also author's path; doap:helper is DOAP's term for a project contributor, so contributors read from helper
rows.comment: documenter, translator and tester are further contributor roles; the consumer may read them too.

rows.source: curated:no cell; DOAP people are foaf:Person nodes and the name most DOAP files give is foaf:name, one string

rows.source: curated:the cell is empty; a Wikidata item has no name property; its name is its label, one per language under labels
rows.comment: English is a choice: a consumer reads the label in the language it wants. aliases lists other names.

rows.source: curated:the cell is empty; software version identifier (P348) holds the version, one statement per release
rows.comment: An item lists every release. Prefer the statement with rank preferred, else the one whose qualifier P577 (publication date) is latest; compare the statement's rank field.

rows.source: curated:the cell says P50, which is not a key of the entity JSON: statements sit under claims, and each statement is a list entry; software items mostly use P178 (developer) instead, so it is the fallback
rows.comment: The value is an item, so mainsnak.datavalue.value.id is a Q id and the person's or organisation's name is in that item's own record. P178 often names an organisation. P2093 (author name string) holds an author with no item; not mapped here.

rows.source: curated:the cell says P735, but P735 sits on the person's item and holds an item of a given name; this record holds only the person's Q id
rows.comment: Fetch the person's entity (claims.P735[]) to read it.

rows.source: curated:the cell says P734, but P734 sits on the person's item and holds an item of a family name; this record holds only the person's Q id
rows.comment: Fetch the person's entity (claims.P734[]) to read it.

rows.source: curated:no cell; the ORCID (P496) sits on the person's item, not on this one
rows.comment: claims.P50[].mainsnak.datavalue.value.id is the person's Wikidata Q id; fetch that entity and read claims.P496[].

rows.source: curated:the cell says P767, which is not a key of the entity JSON: statements sit under claims, and each statement is a list entry
rows.comment: Same shape as author: the value is an item. P767 means contributor to the work; P178 (developer) also exists and the cell does not list it.

rows.source: curated:the cell says P735, but P735 sits on the person's item; this record holds only the person's Q id
rows.comment: Fetch the person's entity to read it.

rows.source: curated:the cell says P734, but P734 sits on the person's item; this record holds only the person's Q id

rows.source: curated:no cell; the ORCID (P496) sits on the person's item, not on this one

rows.source: curated:the cell says P275, which is not a key of the entity JSON; the licence is an item, so its Q id is the value
rows.comment: The value is the Q id of the licence's item; that item's claims.P2479[] (SPDX license ID) gives the SPDX id, for example MIT for Q334661.

rows.source: curated:the cell is empty; DOI (P356) holds a DOI
rows.comment: P356 is an external id; a software item may hold the DOI of a paper about it, so check the DOI resolves to the software.

rows.source: curated:the cell is empty; Software Hash Identifier, SWHID (P6138), holds the Software Heritage id
curated:the cell says P1324, which is not a key of the entity JSON; source code repository URL is a url statement
curated:the cell is empty; a Wikidata item has a short description per language under descriptions
rows.comment: Wikidata descriptions are one short phrase, shorter than a README summary.

rows.source: curated:the cell says P921, which is not a key of the entity JSON; main subject holds items, so the value is a Q id
rows.comment: Wikidata has no free-text keyword property. The label of each Q id is the keyword.

rows.source: curated:the cell says P577, which is not a key of the entity JSON; the date is the time field of a time value
rows.comment: The value looks like +2020-05-01T00:00:00Z; precision (11 = day, 9 = year) says how much of it is real.
